author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Tencent-backed Enflame Technology surged roughly 200% in its Shanghai trading debut Friday after raising 6.12 billion yuan, about $912 million, in one of China’s closely watched AI-chip listings.

The shares were offered at 142.18 yuan, opened at 410 yuan and rose as high as 475 yuan before trading around 430 yuan in the early Reuters report. At that level, the company was valued at about 185 billion yuan. Those figures were time-stamped during the session and should not be read as live prices.

Enflame is developing domestic graphics and AI accelerators as China seeks alternatives to U.S. suppliers. Tencent owns 17.95% of the company and was also responsible for 83.79% of its 2025 revenue, creating both a powerful commercial relationship and a concentration risk.

The chipmaker reported a 2025 net loss of 1.16 billion yuan on revenue of 990.2 million yuan, which rose 37%. IPO proceeds are earmarked for next-generation chips and related development. The first-day jump shows strong demand for the theme, but it does not resolve Enflame’s losses, customer concentration or the execution risks of scaling advanced semiconductor products.
dek: The Tencent-backed AI-chip company opened far above its offer price as investors continued to favor domestic semiconductor listings.
headline: Enflame shares triple in Shanghai debut after $912 million IPO
